## `CoreRegistrySinks`

<a id="cwydeprecations"></a>

## `CwyDeprecations`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Mods.CwyDeprecations` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader`

The runtime half of the [`CwyDeprecatedAttribute`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Mods.md#cwydeprecatedattribute) convention: a deprecated member calls [`CwyDeprecations.Notify`](#cwydeprecations--notify-memberinfo), which finds the calling mod and writes one line per mod per member per session - trace file only for [`DeprecationStage.Notice`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Mods.md#deprecationstage--notice), a `MODS` console line for [`DeprecationStage.Info`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Mods.md#deprecationstage--info), a `MODS` warning for [`DeprecationStage.PendingRemoval`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Mods.md#deprecationstage--pendingremoval) (SMAPI's levels).

The attribute is found where the author put it - on the property of a `get_X`, the event of an `add_X`, the interface member a class method implements ([`DeprecatedMembers`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Mods.md#deprecatedmembers)) - and the stack is walked once per member and calling mod assembly: later calls read one fixed frame and return. Mark a deprecated member `[MethodImpl(MethodImplOptions.NoInlining)]` so that frame is its caller.

<a id="cwydeprecations--count"></a>

### `static int Count { get; }`

How many distinct (mod, member) notices have been written this session.

<a id="cwydeprecations--notify-memberinfo"></a>

### `static void Notify(MemberInfo member)`

Reports a call to the deprecated member `member`, reading its [`CwyDeprecatedAttribute`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Mods.md#cwydeprecatedattribute) - on the member, its property or event, the interface member it implements, or its type. Does nothing when there is none. Never throws.

**Parameters**

- `member`: The deprecated member, normally `MethodBase.GetCurrentMethod()`.

<a id="cwydeprecations--notify-string-string-deprecationstage-string"></a>

### `static void Notify(string member, string since, DeprecationStage stage, string replacement = null)`

Reports a call to a deprecated member, with its values given explicitly. Never throws.

**Parameters**

- `member`: The member, as authors know it, e.g. `ICwyModSatone.SayLegacy`.
- `since`: The API version that deprecated it.
- `stage`: How loudly to announce it.
- `replacement`: What to use instead, or null.

<a id="cwymod"></a>

## `CwyMod`

abstract class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Mods.CwyMod` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader` · mod API

The base class of every code mod. A mod's `entryDll` contains exactly one concrete subclass; the framework creates it with its parameterless constructor and calls [`CwyMod.Entry`](#cwymod--entry) once, in dependency order, on the Unity main thread.

An abstract class rather than an interface so the framework can add members later without breaking a compiled mod.

Everything the mod needs comes through [`ICwyModHelper`](#icwymodhelper): the helper is created for this mod alone, so every log line, event handler, console command, hotkey, config entry and data file carries the mod's id, every call into the mod is wrapped (a throwing mod is logged against its id and the others keep running), and when it stops the framework takes back what it registered through the helper and its Harmony patches (under its id, or declared in its assemblies). Its own threads, objects and files are not taken back. Do not start threads that touch Unity; use [`ICwyModHelper.MainThread`](#icwymodhelper--mainthread). Do not keep a MonoBehaviour of your own: use [`ICwyModEvents.EveryFrame`](#icwymodevents--everyframe).

<a id="cwymod--helper"></a>

### `ICwyModHelper Helper { get; }`

This mod's helper. Set before [`CwyMod.Entry`](#cwymod--entry) runs; reading it in the constructor throws.

**Exceptions**

- `InvalidOperationException`: Read before the framework attached the helper.

<a id="cwymod--log"></a>

### `ICwyModLog Log { get; }`

Shorthand for `Helper.Log`.

<a id="cwymod--manifest"></a>

### `ICwyModManifest Manifest { get; }`

Shorthand for `Helper.Manifest`.

<a id="cwymod--entry"></a>

### `abstract void Entry(ICwyModHelper helper)`

Called once when the mod loads, on the main thread, after every mod it depends on has entered. Register what you need here: events, commands, hotkeys, config. The room and the player's data are usually not ready yet; subscribe to `RoomReady` for that. An exception marks the mod failed; the framework then takes back what it registered through the helper and removes its Harmony patches (see [`ICwyModHelper.Harmony`](#icwymodhelper--harmony)).

**Parameters**

- `helper`: This mod's helper (also available as [`CwyMod.Helper`](#cwymod--helper)).

<a id="cwymod--getapi"></a>

### `virtual object GetApi()`

The object other mods get from `helper.ModRegistry.GetApi<T>("your.id")`, or null (the default) for none. Called once, after every mod's [`CwyMod.Entry`](#cwymod--entry). Make it implement a public interface the other mod references.

<a id="cwymod--onshutdown"></a>

### `virtual void OnShutdown()`

Called once when the game quits, in reverse load order, on the main thread. Save what you need; subscriptions are removed by the framework afterwards.

<a id="icwymodactions"></a>

## `ICwyModActions`

interface · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Mods.ICwyModActions` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader` · mod API

Extends: [`ICwyModFacet`](#icwymodfacet)

Actions: the semantic game actions (music, pomodoro, panels, room, todos ...) that the console, scripts and the local API also use, and a mod's own actions for them. Listing and registering always work; running needs the action runner, which the framework installs while `[Actions] Enabled` is true - otherwise [`ICwyModActions.RunAsync`](#icwymodactions--runasync) answers [`ActionStatus.NotAvailable`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Actions.md#actionstatus--notavailable). Every run goes through the same schema check, tier gate ([`ActionGate`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Actions.md#actiongate)), confirmation and `ACTION` audit line as the API, with this mod as a [`ActionCaller.Mod`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Actions.md#actioncaller--mod) caller; the handler runs in this mod's dispatcher lane. For an LLM tool list, `ActionToolSchema.BuildAll(helper.Actions.List())` gives each action's name, description, tier hints and argument schema. Only the framework implements this interface.

<a id="icwymodactions--list"></a>

### `IReadOnlyList<ActionDescriptor> List()`

Every registered action, sorted by name.

<a id="icwymodactions--register"></a>

### `CwyRegistration Register(ActionDescriptor descriptor, ActionHandler handler)`

Publishes an action of this mod's own to the console (`act run`), scripts (`cwy.do`) and the local API. The name must start with `<modId>.`. The handler runs on the main thread with this mod's attribution; if it throws, the call ends as [`ActionStatus.Failed`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Actions.md#actionstatus--failed).

**Parameters**

- `descriptor`: What the action is.
- `handler`: What runs it.

**Returns:** The handle; refused (with the reason) when the name is unusable or taken.

<a id="icwymodactions--runasync"></a>

### `Task<ActionResult> RunAsync(string name, ActionArgs args = null, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)`

Runs an action as this mod. Never faults: every outcome, including "not available", is an [`ActionResult`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Actions.md#actionresult). The main-thread hop waits at most 2 s. Await it or continue from it; never wait for it synchronously on the main thread (the hop is queued for a later frame, so the wait would end as TimedOut).

**Parameters**

- `name`: The action name, e.g. `music.play`.
- `args`: Its arguments; null for none.
- `cancellationToken`: Stops waiting.

<a id="icwymodapi"></a>

## `ICwyModApi`

interface · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Mods.ICwyModApi` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader` · mod API

Extends: [`ICwyModFacet`](#icwymodfacet)

Api: the local game API that programs on this computer (an MCP server, an AI companion, sidecars) use - state, events and actions over HTTP on the literal loopback address `127.0.0.1:7870` only, with a per-launch access key in an owner-only file. Off by default (`[Api] Enabled=false`: no listener, no port, no key file). A mod does not serve requests itself: it publishes actions through the Actions facet, and the API lists and runs them like the framework's own. The backend is installed by the `CwyLs.ModLoader.Api` plugin with `ModFacetBackends.Use<ICwyModApi>`; only the framework implements this interface. Wire reference: `src/CwyLs.ModLoader.Core/Api/README.md`.

<a id="icwymodapi--endpoint"></a>

### `string Endpoint { get; }`

The base address while listening, e.g. `http://127.0.0.1:7870/`; empty otherwise. The access key is never exposed here.

<a id="icwymodapi--isrunning"></a>

### `bool IsRunning { get; }`

True while the API is listening; false when it is off or the plugin is not installed.

<a id="icwymodaudio"></a>

## `ICwyModAudio`

interface · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Mods.ICwyModAudio` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader` · mod API

Extends: [`ICwyModFacet`](#icwymodfacet)

Audio: the game's replaceable sound rows - ambient loops, ambient one-shots, system and timer sounds, story music - and the pack music tracks. Packs replace rows with files in `audio/ambient/`, `audio/ambient_se/`, `audio/se/system/`, `audio/se/timer/`, `audio/direction_music/` and add tracks with `audio/music/` (+ `_tracks.json`); a code mod is a pack too, so its own folders work the same way. This facet adds runtime replacements and the A/B switch. Main thread. Only the framework implements this interface.

Paid content is never replaced: story music that plays a track of the game's soundtrack (sold as Steam DLC 3718890) is refused, as the console and [`AudioRowInfo.Refusal`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Audio.md#audiorowinfo--refusal) say. Voice clips stay in the Satone facet.

<a id="icwymodaudio--musictracks"></a>

### `IReadOnlyList<MusicTrackInfo> MusicTracks()`

The pack music tracks, loaded or not, listed or not. A detached copy.

<a id="icwymodaudio--reload"></a>

### `void Reload()`

Re-reads the packs' audio files and applies them again (changed files are reloaded).

<a id="icwymodaudio--replaceclip"></a>

### `CwyRegistration ReplaceClip(string row, AudioClip clip)`

Replaces a row's clip from code; beats every pack. The clip is renamed to the game clip's name (the game's audio managers look players up by name). Dispose the handle to take it back.

**Parameters**

- `row`: A row key (`ambient/LightRain`), or a row name once the game's data is loaded (`LightRain`).
- `clip`: The clip; it must stay alive while registered.

**Returns:** The handle; refused (with the reason) for an unknown row, a paid row, or when audio is off.

<a id="icwymodaudio--rows"></a>

### `IReadOnlyList<AudioRowInfo> Rows()`

Every game sound row with its replacement, selection and what is playing. A detached copy; empty before the game's data is loaded.

<a id="icwymodaudio--select"></a>

### `AudioSwitchResult Select(string rows, AudioVariant? variant)`

The A/B switch: plays the game's clip or the replacement for the named rows; a playing loop moves to the other clip at the same position.

**Parameters**

- `rows`: A row, a table (`ambient`) or `all`.
- `variant`: Which clip; null toggles.

**Returns:** Per-row outcomes, or the problem.

## `ICwyModConditions`

interface · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Mods.ICwyModConditions` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader` · mod API

Extends: [`ICwyModFacet`](#icwymodfacet)

Conditions: the `when` grammar packs use (time, weekday, pomodoro, language, flags ...), for a mod's own decisions, plus tokens a mod adds for packs to use (`<modId>/<name>`). Parsing always works; evaluating needs the condition provider, which the framework installs - until then [`ICwyModConditions.Evaluate`](#icwymodconditions--evaluate-conditionset) answers [`ConditionOutcome.Unavailable`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Conditions.md#conditionoutcome--unavailable) for anything but an empty set. Only the framework implements this interface. Grammar: `src/CwyLs.ModLoader.Core/Conditions/README.md`.

<a id="icwymodconditions--evaluate-conditionset"></a>

### `ConditionResult Evaluate(ConditionSet conditions)`

Evaluates a set now. Main thread. Never throws.

**Parameters**

- `conditions`: The set.

**Returns:** Met, NotMet, Unavailable or Invalid, with the reason; only Met means "apply".

<a id="icwymodconditions--evaluate-object"></a>

### `ConditionResult Evaluate(object when)`

Parses and evaluates in one call; a syntax problem is [`ConditionOutcome.Invalid`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Conditions.md#conditionoutcome--invalid).

**Parameters**

- `when`: The block.

<a id="icwymodconditions--notifytokenchanged"></a>

### `void NotifyTokenChanged(string name)`

Says one of this mod's tokens changed, so conditions that use it are checked again.

**Parameters**

- `name`: The name after the slash.

<a id="icwymodconditions--onchanged"></a>

### `IDisposable OnChanged(Action<ConditionsChanged> handler)`

Called whenever conditions may answer differently ([`ConditionsChanged`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Conditions.md#conditionschanged)). Main thread.

**Parameters**

- `handler`: Your callback.

**Returns:** Dispose to unsubscribe.

<a id="icwymodconditions--parse"></a>

### `ConditionParseResult Parse(object when)`

Parses a `when` block (a parsed JSON object, or any string-keyed dictionary; null = no conditions).

**Parameters**

- `when`: The block.

**Returns:** The set, or every syntax problem.

<a id="icwymodconditions--registertoken"></a>

### `CwyRegistration RegisterToken(string name, ConditionValueKind kind, string description, Func<string, IReadOnlyList<string>> values, ConditionArgumentRule argument = ConditionArgumentRule.None)`

Adds a token packs can test as `<modId>/<name>`. Its values come from `values`, called on the main thread with the clause's argument (or null); return null while the value is not known. Call [`ICwyModConditions.NotifyTokenChanged`](#icwymodconditions--notifytokenchanged) when it changes.

**Parameters**

- `name`: The name after the slash: a letter, then letters, digits or `_`.
- `kind`: How its values compare.
- `description`: One sentence for `cond tokens`.
- `values`: The current values for an argument.
- `argument`: Whether it takes an argument after a colon.

**Returns:** The handle; refused (with the reason) when the name is unusable or taken.

## `ICwyModConsole`

interface · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Mods.ICwyModConsole` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader` · mod API

Console commands (Ctrl+Shift+C). A mod cannot replace a command someone else registered.

<a id="icwymodconsole--register"></a>

### `CwyRegistration Register(string name, string description, string usage, Func<IReadOnlyList<string>, string> handler)`

Registers a command, listed under the mod's id in `help`.

**Parameters**

- `name`: What the player types; no spaces.

- `usage`: The argument shape, e.g. `hello [name]`; also drives Tab completion.

<a id="icwymoddata"></a>

## `ICwyModData`

interface · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Mods.ICwyModData` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader` · mod API

A mod's own persistent files in `BepInEx/data/mods/<id>/`. A key is a file name: letters, digits, `_ . -`, 1 to 64 characters, not starting with a dot, not a Windows device name (`con`, `nul.txt`, `com1` ...) and not ending in a dot. Keys are case-insensitive: `Save.json` and `save.json` are one key, stored in lower case, on every operating system. A write goes to a temporary file, is flushed to disk, then replaces the real file, so a crash never leaves half a file under the key. Thread-safe.

<a id="icwymoddata--directorypath"></a>

### `string DirectoryPath { get; }`

Absolute path of the folder (created on the first write).

<a id="icwymoddata--delete"></a>

### `bool Delete(string key)`

Deletes the file.

**Parameters**

- `key`: A data key.

**Returns:** True when a file was deleted.

<a id="icwymoddata--exists"></a>

### `bool Exists(string key)`

True when the key has a file.

**Parameters**

- `key`: A data key.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentException`: The key breaks the naming rule.

<a id="icwymoddata--keys"></a>

### `IReadOnlyList<string> Keys()`

Every key that has a file, in lower case, sorted.

<a id="icwymoddata--readjson"></a>

### `object ReadJson(string key)`

The file parsed as strict JSON: `JsonObject`, lists, strings, `long`/`double`, booleans or null; null when the file does not exist.

**Parameters**

- `key`: A data key.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentException`: The key breaks the naming rule.
- [`JsonParseException`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Json.md#jsonparseexception): The file is not valid JSON (the message has line:column).

<a id="icwymoddata--readtext"></a>

### `string ReadText(string key)`

The file's text (UTF-8), or null when it does not exist.

**Parameters**

- `key`: A data key.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentException`: The key breaks the naming rule.

<a id="icwymoddata--writejson"></a>

### `void WriteJson(string key, object value)`

Writes `value` as JSON (public properties and fields, depth 12), atomically.

**Parameters**

- `key`: A data key.
- `value`: The value.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentException`: The key breaks the naming rule.

<a id="icwymoddata--writetext"></a>

### `void WriteText(string key, string text)`

Writes the file atomically (UTF-8, no BOM).

**Parameters**

- `key`: A data key.
- `text`: The content; null writes an empty file.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentException`: The key breaks the naming rule.

<a id="icwymodharmony"></a>

## `ICwyModHarmony`

interface · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Mods.ICwyModHarmony` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader` · mod API

Extends: [`ICwyModFacet`](#icwymodfacet)

Harmony: a HarmonyX instance whose id is this mod's id, owned by the framework. When the mod fails in its constructor or `Entry`, and when the game quits, the framework removes every patch made under that id **and** every patch whose patch method is declared in one of the mod's own assemblies, under any id - so a failed mod leaves no patch of its behind. It never calls an id-less `UnpatchAll`. Only the framework implements this interface.

A mod may still create its own `new Harmony("some.id")`; patch methods declared in its assemblies are taken back all the same. The framework cannot catch an exception inside a patch: catch it there and fall back to the original.

<a id="icwymodharmony--id"></a>

### `string Id { get; }`

The Harmony id: the mod's id.

<a id="icwymodharmony--instance"></a>

### `Harmony Instance { get; }`

The instance, created on first use. Patch through it: `Instance.Patch(original, prefix: ...)`.

**Exceptions**

- `InvalidOperationException`: The mod is not running (failed or shut down).

<a id="icwymodharmony--getpatchedmethods"></a>

### `IReadOnlyList<MethodBase> GetPatchedMethods()`

The original methods patched under this id.

<a id="icwymodharmony--patchall"></a>

### `void PatchAll()`

Applies every `[HarmonyPatch]` class in the mod's own entry assembly (not the caller's, which through this helper would be the framework). Throws what Harmony throws, so a failure in `Entry` fails the mod and the framework removes whatever was already applied.

**Exceptions**

- `InvalidOperationException`: The mod is not running, or its assembly is not known.

<a id="icwymodharmony--unpatchself"></a>

### `void UnpatchSelf()`

Removes every patch made under this id now (the mod keeps running).

<a id="icwymodinput"></a>

## `ICwyModInput`

interface · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Mods.ICwyModInput` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader` · mod API

Hotkeys. The framework id of a mod's hotkey is `mod:<modId>/<id>` - a separator no mod or framework id contains, so it can never collide with `console.toggle` or another mod's key. Chords are bound in the mod's config.

<a id="icwymodinput--register"></a>

### `CwyRegistration Register(string id, string description, string primaryChord, string alternateChord, Action onPressed)`

Registers a function with a primary and an optional alternate chord, written like `Ctrl+Shift+H` or `F7`. Keys never fire while a text field has focus. The player can rebind both in `BepInEx/config/cwy.mod.<id>.cfg`, section `[Hotkeys]`.

**Parameters**

- `id`: Short id, e.g. `greet`; letters, digits, `. _ -`.
- `description`: One sentence: what pressing it does.
- `primaryChord`: Default primary chord, e.g. `Ctrl+Shift+H`.
- `alternateChord`: Default alternate chord, or null for none.
- `onPressed`: What to run, on the main thread.

**Returns:** The handle (name `mod:<modId>/<id>`); refused, with the reason, when the id or a chord is unusable (also logged). Disposing it stops the callback; the key stays listed in the hotkey table until the game restarts.

<a id="icwymodmainthread"></a>

## `ICwyModMainThread`

interface · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Mods.ICwyModMainThread` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader` · mod API

The shared main-thread dispatcher, with the mod as owner of its work.

<a id="icwymodmainthread--ismainthread"></a>

### `bool IsMainThread { get; }`

True on Unity's main thread.

<a id="icwymodmainthread--now"></a>

### `double Now { get; }`

Monotonic seconds; safe on any thread.

<a id="icwymodmainthread--invoke-string-action-timespan"></a>

### `void Invoke(string label, Action work, TimeSpan timeout)`

Runs work on the main thread and blocks until it is done (inline on the main thread).

**Parameters**

- `label`: What the work is.
- `work`: The work; its exception is rethrown to the caller.
- `timeout`: How long a background caller waits.

**Exceptions**

- `TimeoutException`: The main thread did not run it in time.
- [`MainThreadRejectedException`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Threading.md#mainthreadrejectedexception): The framework refused it (queue full, mod not running).

<a id="icwymodmainthread--invoke-string-func-t-timespan"></a>

### `T Invoke<T>(string label, Func<T> work, TimeSpan timeout)`

Runs a function on the main thread and blocks for it (inline on the main thread).

**Type parameters**

- `T`: The result type.

**Parameters**

- `label`: What the work is.
- `work`: The function.
- `timeout`: How long a background caller waits.

**Exceptions**

- `TimeoutException`: The main thread did not run it in time.
- [`MainThreadRejectedException`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Threading.md#mainthreadrejectedexception): The framework refused it (queue full, mod not running).

<a id="icwymodmainthread--invokeasync-string-action-timespan-cancellationtoken"></a>

### `Task InvokeAsync(string label, Action work, TimeSpan? timeout = null, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)`

Runs work on the main thread; the task faults with its exception, a `TimeoutException`, or a [`MainThreadRejectedException`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Threading.md#mainthreadrejectedexception) when the framework refused it (queue full, mod not running).

**Parameters**

- `label`: What the work is.
- `work`: The work.
- `timeout`: Wall-clock limit on your side; null means the framework default (2 s), `Timeout.InfiniteTimeSpan` waits forever. Work not started by then is skipped, never run late.
- `cancellationToken`: Stops the wait.

<a id="icwymodmainthread--invokeasync-string-func-t-timespan-cancellationtoken"></a>

### `Task<T> InvokeAsync<T>(string label, Func<T> work, TimeSpan? timeout = null, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)`

Runs a function on the main thread and returns its result through a task.

**Type parameters**

- `T`: The result type.

**Parameters**

- `label`: What the work is.
- `work`: The function.
- `timeout`: Wall-clock limit on your side; null means the framework default (2 s).
- `cancellationToken`: Stops the wait.

<a id="icwymodmainthread--post"></a>

### `bool Post(string label, Action work)`

Queues work for the next frame. Exceptions are logged against the mod.

**Parameters**

- `label`: What the work is.
- `work`: The work.

**Returns:** False when the mod's queue is full.

<a id="icwymodmainthread--postafter"></a>

### `DelayedWork PostAfter(double seconds, string label, Action work)`

Runs work on the main thread after a real-time delay.

**Parameters**

- `seconds`: The delay; zero or less runs it on the next frame.
- `label`: What the work is.
- `work`: The work.

**Returns:** A handle: dispose it (or `Cancel()`) to drop the work before it runs. `IsAccepted` is false when the mod's delayed queue was full (logged).

**Exceptions**

- [`MainThreadRejectedException`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Threading.md#mainthreadrejectedexception): The mod is not running any more.

<a id="icwymodmainthread--runorpost"></a>

### `bool RunOrPost(string label, Action work)`

Runs work now on the main thread, otherwise queues it.

**Parameters**

- `label`: What the work is.
- `work`: The work.

## `ModBackends`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Mods.ModBackends` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader`

Where the game-specific facets of the mod helper come from. CwyLs.ModLoader cannot reference the game, so the adapter plugins (CwyLs.ModLoader.Bulbul, CwyLs.ModLoader.Bulbul.Data) register their implementations here from their `Awake`, which runs before any mod loads. A facet whose backend was never registered reports `IsAvailable = false`.

API freeze: the `Use*` registrations are internal, visible only to the framework's own assemblies (`AssemblyInfo.cs`), so a mod cannot replace a backend.

<a id="modfacetbackends"></a>

## `ModFacetBackends`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Mods.ModFacetBackends` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader`

Where the game-side backends of the Phases D-S facets come from (EditData, Audio, UiSkin, Camera, VoiceStream, Mic, Api). The feature that implements a facet registers its backend from its own `Initialize`, which runs in a plugin's `Awake` before any mod loads: `ModFacetBackends.Use<ICwyModAudio>("audio", backend)`. A facet with no backend reports `IsAvailable = false` and its documented "not available" status.

One generic table instead of a property per facet so a new feature never edits a shared file to plug in. The original facets (events, Satone, game data, language, windows) keep their typed slots in [`ModBackends`](#modbackends); Conditions, Actions and Scenes are backed by the Core registries (`ConditionRegistry`, `ActionServices`, `ScenarioCommandRegistry`).

The facets that have a backend, e.g. `audio,uiSkin`; empty when none.

The backend of one facet, or null when none is installed.

- `T`: The facet interface.

<a id="modloader"></a>

## `ModLoader`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Mods.ModLoader` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader`

The code-mod loader: after the packs resolve, it loads every pack with an `entryDll` in dependency order, creates its one [`CwyMod`](#cwymod) subclass and calls [`CwyMod.Entry`](#cwymod--entry), then collects the mods' APIs and raises the mods-ready signal.

**When.** On the first frame of the shared main-thread host, i.e. after every BepInEx plugin's `Awake` has run, so the game adapter has registered the game-specific facets ([`ModBackends`](#modbackends)). The plugin component itself is gone by then in this game; the host is a hidden `DontDestroyOnLoad` object.

**Isolation.** Every step that touches mod code is wrapped: a refused mod is [`ModState.Skipped`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Mods.md#modstate--skipped) with a reason, a mod whose constructor or `Entry` throws is [`ModState.Failed`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Mods.md#modstate--failed) (one `MODS` line, full stack in the trace file) and everything it registered is taken back - its helper registrations are disposed, and its Harmony patches removed (`UnpatchSelf()` for the mod id plus every patch whose patch method is declared in one of the mod's assemblies; never an id-less `UnpatchAll`) - and mods that require it are skipped as [`ModSkipReason.DependencyFailed`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Mods.md#modskipreason--dependencyfailed). An unexpected failure of the loader itself skips only that mod ([`ModSkipReason.AssemblyLoadFailed`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Mods.md#modskipreason--assemblyloadfailed)). The rest keep loading.

**No unload.** Mono cannot unload an assembly, so a changed mod DLL needs a game restart; `packs rescan` does not reload code. A DLL loaded from a file stays memory-mapped: never overwrite a mod DLL while the game runs (deploy with the game closed).

**Binding**: one `AssemblyResolve` handler, installed before any mod type is touched, answers in the order of [`ModAssemblyResolver`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Mods.md#modassemblyresolver): an already-loaded assembly of that name for anyone; for a mod's assembly, its own folder and then the other mod folders; for an unknown requester, a mod folder only when exactly one has the name; for the game, a plugin or the framework, never a mod folder. Every DLL it loads from a mod folder is mapped to that mod. Never a framework, game, BepInEx or Harmony name, nor another mod's entry DLL, from a mod folder. A second copy of an assembly (same name, or same build) is refused, because HarmonyX would cross-wire its patches. Deciding and loading happen under one lock.

<a id="modloader--configkeyassemblyload"></a>

### `const string ConfigKeyAssemblyLoad = "AssemblyLoad"`

Config key of the assembly load mode (troubleshooting switch).

<a id="modloader--configkeyenabled"></a>

### `const string ConfigKeyEnabled = "Enabled"`

Config key of the master switch.

<a id="modloader--configsection"></a>

### `const string ConfigSection = "Mods"`

Config section of the loader settings (in the framework's .cfg).

How mod assemblies are read (`[Mods] AssemblyLoad`, default LoadFrom).

<a id="modloader--enabled"></a>

### `static bool Enabled { get; }`

True when code mods are loaded at all (`[Mods] Enabled`, default true).
